record.original_question: Let A,B,C⊆N satisfy A=B∪C and B∩C=∅. For any X⊆N, let R_d(X)={(upper_d(D), lower_d(D)): D⊆X} be the density set relative to asymptotic density d, where upper_d and lower_d are upper and lower asymptotic densities. Give a complete characterization, preferably by necessary and sufficient properties, of the triples of density sets R_d(A), R_d(B), and R_d(C) that can occur for such a disjoint decomposition.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a set $X\subseteq\mathbb{N}$, denote by 
$$\overline{d}(X)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{|X\cap[1,n]|}{n},\qquad \underline{d}(X)=\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{|X\cap[1,n]|}{n}$$
the upper and lower asymptotic densities of $X$. For $X\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ define the density set
$$R_d(X)=\{(\overline{d}(D),\underline{d}(D)):D\subseteq X\}\subseteq[0,1]^2.$$
Suppose $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $A=B\cup C$ and $B\cap C=\emptyset$. Give a complete characterization, by necessary and sufficient conditions, of all triples $(R_d(A),R_d(B),R_d(C))$ of subsets of $[0,1]^2$ that arise from such disjoint decompositions. That is, find a list of properties relating the three sets $R_d(A)$, $R_d(B)$, $R_d(C)$, and prove that these properties hold exactly for triples arising from a partition $A=B\sqcup C$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published characterization of the triples $(R_d(A),R_d(B),R_d(C))$ for disjoint unions $A=B\sqcup C$ appears in the literature. Related work on density sets and upper/lower densities (e.g., by Leonetti and Tringali) develops the framework of $R_d(X)$ but does not resolve this characterization problem, which appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the notions of upper and lower density
status_evidence.snippet: Develops axiomatic framework for upper and lower densities and studies properties of associated density sets.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work on density sets exists but does not give the disjoint-union characterization.

status_evidence.title: Asymptotic density of A⊂ℕ and density of the ratio set R(A)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies density sets associated with subsets of natural numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Related density-set studies do not address the triple characterization for disjoint unions.
